events.title: OpenAI IPO Closing Market Cap
events.description:
This market will resolve based on OpenAI's market capitalization at the closing price on its first day of trading.

If no IPO occurs by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "No IPO by December 31, 2027".

Market capitalization expresses the monetary value of a company’s outstanding shares, stated in its pricing currency. It is calculated as the number of shares outstanding multiplied by the closing share price on the first trading day.

If the relevant value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Resolution will be based on the primary exchange’s official listing page. In the event that the relevant figure is not displayed, another reliable source will be used.

In the event of an interruption in the course of the normal trading session on OpenAI’s first day of trading (e.g., a circuit breaker or half-day), the market will resolve according to the official closing price of the abbreviated session. If no such official closing price is published, the market will resolve according to the next trading day on which an official closing price is published, treating that as the first day of trading for purposes of this market.

events.title: OpenAI announces another Millennium Prize solution by...?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI, or an official representative of OpenAI, announces that OpenAI has solved any of the qualifying Millennium Prize Problems between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The qualifying problems are the Riemann Hypothesis, P versus NP, the Yang-Mills existence and mass gap problem, the Hodge Conjecture, and the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture (https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/). Announcements concerning the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem will not qualify.

A qualifying announcement must express that the problem has been solved; announcements of partial results or progress toward a solution will not qualify. The announcement must present the solution as the work of OpenAI, its researchers, or its models, alone or jointly with outside researchers. An announcement that only credits or congratulates outside researchers, including researchers who used OpenAI's models, compute, or research credits, will not qualify. No further confirmation from Clay Math Institute or any other organization is required.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

NPM Prices are published for trading days only and are updated once daily at 1:00 PM ET on the following calendar day.

If NPM has not published relevant data for the specified date by 1:00 PM ET on January 1, 2027, this market may remain open until 11:59 PM ET on January 4, 2027. If no further data is released by that time, the market will resolve according to the data available.

If NPM ceases publishing relevant data prior to the specified date, this market will resolve based on the NPM data published prior to the cessation of coverage, as well as applicable public market capitalization data following an IPO or direct listing.

If a private company completes an IPO or direct listing prior to the specified date, this market will resolve according to the company’s public market capitalization at the market close of the specified date or the most recent trading day.

Public market capitalization will be determined using the final official regular-hour trading price published for the company’s primary listed common equity on its primary exchange for the specified date or the most recent trading day, multiplied by the company’s total outstanding common shares at the relevant time.

If the listed company merges with or acquires another entity and remains the parent company, no change to resolution methodology applies.

If a listed company is acquired, merges into another entity and is no longer the surviving parent company, or otherwise ceases to exist as an independent entity prior to the end of the period, only the last NPM valuation and applicable public market capitalization achieved prior to completion of the transaction will be considered for resolution. No transaction, acquisition, or merger consideration will be considered for resolution.

The resolution source for this market is NPM data published here (https://fe.secondmarket.com/companies/company-30839e0b-2730-4495-839f-1bf638fa9cca/data?return_url=https://polymarket.com/finance/privates) and here (https://fe.secondmarket.com/companies/company-3e197763-4ff8-4d8c-bd1f-cc2792937757/data?return_url=https://polymarket.com/finance/privates). Revisions to previously published NPM data made after their initial release will not be considered, unless made to correct clearly erroneous data.

The primary resolution source will be official information from Anthropic, OpenAI, the relevant governance body, or Jensen Huang; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events.title: Who will the OpenAI spy be accused of working for in 2026?
events.description:
On October 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice announced that Abdulrahman Alfozan, an OpenAI employee and Saudi national, had been arrested and charged after allegedly installing a covert audio recording device in an executive conference room at OpenAI's San Francisco offices (see: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/saudi-national-arrested-installing-surreptitious-audio-recording-device-openai).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. federal government or OpenAI publicly alleges that Abdulrahman Alfozan acted on behalf of the listed entity in connection with this incident between market creation and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For listed countries, the alleged conduct must be attributed to the government of the listed country, its intelligence or security services, or a state-affiliated entity of the listed country. Alfozan's nationality alone will not qualify.

For listed companies or individuals, the alleged conduct must be attributed to the listed company, its subsidiaries, or the listed individual.

A qualifying allegation must definitively state that Alfozan acted on behalf of, or under the direction, control, or sponsorship of, the listed entity. Statements that merely speculate about or suggest possible ties, or that describe only contact, cooperation, or association with the listed entity, will not qualify.

Qualifying allegations include charging documents, court filings, and on-the-record statements by the U.S. Department of Justice, the FBI, or other U.S. federal agencies or their authorized representatives acting in an official capacity, as well as official statements by OpenAI.

Once a qualifying allegation has been made, no subsequent retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government and OpenAI.

This market will resolve according to the calendar month (ET) of OpenAI's IPO date, as defined below.

The "Pricing Prospectus" is the first final prospectus for the IPO filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) through its EDGAR system under Rule 424(b) under the Securities Act of 1933. A later prospectus or prospectus supplement, including one for an increase in the size of the offering or a change in the offering price, does not replace it.

OpenAI's IPO is considered completed only when all three of the following have occurred: (i) the SEC has declared OpenAI's registration statement for the offering effective; (ii) a Qualifying Exchange has approved OpenAI's common equity securities for listing; and (iii) the offering has been priced, as shown by the Pricing Prospectus stating the number of shares offered and the offering price. A "Qualifying Exchange" is the New York Stock Exchange, NYSE American, the Nasdaq Stock Market or Cboe BZX Exchange, and no other. The IPO date is the date stated on the cover of the Pricing Prospectus, read as a date in ET, provided that the events in (i) and (ii) occurred on or before that date. A registration statement declared effective, or a listing approval, without pricing does not count, and neither does a preliminary prospectus published at the start of the marketing of the offering.

Only the IPO date determines the resolving month; the date of the first trade in OpenAI's shares in secondary trading on an exchange does not. An IPO whose IPO date falls on the last day of a month resolves to that month even if its shares first trade on an exchange in the following month. A completed IPO counts even if the offering is later withdrawn or the shares do not begin trading.

Only a traditional IPO qualifies: a priced, underwritten offering of newly issued common equity securities of OpenAI, or of American depositary shares representing them, sold to the public for cash under a registration statement on Form S-1 or Form F-1. An offering in which selling stockholders also sell shares qualifies if it includes newly issued shares sold by OpenAI. It must be the first public offering and listing of OpenAI's common equity securities on any securities exchange. An IPO by a parent or holding company formed to hold all or substantially all of OpenAI's business counts as an IPO by OpenAI; an IPO by a subsidiary or separated business of OpenAI does not.

Direct listings, mergers with special purpose acquisition companies (SPACs), reverse mergers, private placements, offerings limited to institutional or accredited investors, and any listing without an underwritten, SEC-registered offering of new shares are not IPOs. Media reports, announcements of an intention to go public, and the public filing of a registration statement do not count.

If OpenAI's IPO is priced but the Pricing Prospectus has not been published on EDGAR by the end of the pricing day, this market will wait for it until 11:59 PM ET on the second business day after the end of the month in which the IPO was priced.

If OpenAI's IPO date falls on or before December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to "December 2026 or earlier".

If OpenAI's IPO date does not fall on or before December 31, 2027, or if before then OpenAI is acquired by or merged into another entity (other than a holding company formed for the purpose of its IPO), its equity securities become listed or publicly traded other than through a qualifying IPO, or it otherwise permanently ceases to be able to complete an IPO, this market will resolve to "No IPO before 2028".

The primary resolution source will be the SEC's EDGAR system, for the Pricing Prospectus, the registration statement and the notice that the SEC has declared it effective, and the Qualifying Exchange's certification approving OpenAI's securities for listing, together with the Qualifying Exchange's official notice of the listing. OpenAI's official announcements and a consensus of credible reporting may be used only if those sources have not published the relevant filing or notice within two business days after the event is otherwise public.

events.title: OpenAI announces bankruptcy by...?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI announces that it will file for bankruptcy or has filed for bankruptcy of any variety by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. An announcement will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if or when the actual filing occurs. The announcement must be made through any of their official or verified channels, as a recorded or written statement by their CEO, legal representation, or other individual or team which officially represents OpenAI. A definitive consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

"OpenAI" refers to OpenAI Group PBC, the company that holds the OpenAI business and is controlled by the OpenAI Foundation, its operating subsidiary OpenAI OpCo, LLC, or any other entity that is controlled by, or is under common control with, OpenAI Group PBC and that holds, directly or indirectly, all or substantially all of OpenAI's business and assets at the time of the filing or announcement. Unless named above, foreign entities, financing entities, special purpose vehicles, and entities used to separate specific legal liabilities will not qualify, even if they meet that test.

A filing for bankruptcy means a petition by an entity this market refers to (each, a "covered entity") under Chapter 7 or Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code, or a bankruptcy case for a covered entity filed in a court outside the United States under that country's bankruptcy or insolvency law, including a court-appointed administration. A petition filed against a covered entity by its creditors will qualify only if the court enters an order for relief on that petition by the listed date.

An announcement must state that a covered entity has decided to file for bankruptcy, or has filed for bankruptcy. Statements that the company is considering, exploring, or open to bankruptcy, or that bankruptcy is one of several options, will not qualify.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may be used to confirm that a qualifying announcement or filing occurred. Reports citing unnamed sources that a covered entity plans or is preparing to file will not qualify on their own.

Once a qualifying filing or announcement occurs, this market will resolve to "Yes" even if the petition is later withdrawn, dismissed, or converted, or the company later reverses its decision.

The following will not qualify on their own: a missed payment or other default on debt; a breach of a loan covenant; foreclosure or other enforcement action by creditors; a credit rating downgrade; a debt exchange or other restructuring agreed outside of court; the appointment of a receiver; and an assignment for the benefit of creditors.

If a covered entity stops existing because of a merger or similar transaction, it will no longer be a covered entity. If, after the merger, no covered entity remains, this market will resolve to "No". If the transaction only changes a covered entity's name, state of incorporation, or legal form, or places a new holding company over the same business, the resulting entity will be treated as that covered entity.

A filing occurs at the time recorded by the court. An announcement occurs at the time it is first published by a covered entity or its representative.
